definitions.explanation: A male relative who is like an older brother but not by blood — typically a spouse's older brother, or a stepbrother who is older. Composed of 義 (righteousness/adopted) + 兄 (older brother). A formal term used in writing and official contexts.

examples.japanese: {義兄|ぎけい}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{医者|いしゃ}→医者：02847_isha⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦している→する：00392_suru⟧。
⟦{結婚式|けっこんしき}→結婚式：05493_kekkonshiki⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧{義兄|ぎけい}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦スピーチ→スピーチ：03852_supiichi⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{頼|たの}まれた→頼む：01104_tanomu⟧。
examples.english: I was asked by my brother-in-law to give a speech at the wedding.

examples.japanese: {義兄|ぎけい}⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{年|とし}→年：00486_toshi⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦{近|ちか}い→近い：00530_chikai⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦よく→よく：00601_yoku⟧⟦{一緒|いっしょ}→一緒：02848_issho⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{遊|あそ}んでいた→遊ぶ：00550_asobu⟧。
examples.english: Since my stepbrother and I are close in age, we often played together growing up.

notes:
USAGE:
{義兄|ぎけい} is a formal, written term. In everyday conversation, people typically say お{義兄|にい}さん or ⟦{義理|ぎり}→義理：10891_giri⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{兄|あに}→兄：00570_ani⟧. The {義|ぎ} prefix indicates a family relationship by marriage or adoption rather than by blood.

RELATED WORDS:
- ⟦{義弟|ぎてい}→義弟：13981_gitei⟧ (younger brother-in-law)
- ⟦{義姉|ぎし}→義姉：17835_gishi⟧ (older sister-in-law)
- ⟦{義妹|ぎまい}→義妹：18404_gimai⟧ (younger sister-in-law)
- ⟦{義父|ぎふ}→義父：06725_gifu⟧ (father-in-law)
- ⟦{義母|ぎぼ}→義母：06724_gibo⟧ (mother-in-law)

The spoken form お{義兄|にい}さん uses the kun'yomi reading and is warmer and more familiar.
